text:
oliver: Heads up — seeing a p95 jump (~45%) on canary for v2.3.1 in eu-west during the 03:00 deploy window. Fastpath token latency mostly. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/rt/canary/2312 (open)
maya: looking now. which model / seq distro was targeted in the canary? any recent runtime kernel patches landed last night?
oliver: model=redwood-open-7b, batch=1, seq_dist skew to 128-256. yes @lucas pushed a kernel/alloc tweak at 22:10UTC last night. not sure if it hit canary hosts.
lucas: I shipped the allocator patch; it touched tcmalloc flags. rolling update was staged to canary subset only. grabbing logs and perf data now.
kevin: can we isolate eu-west canary nodes and stop traffic while we profile? prefer hold vs immediate rollback until we have profiles.
maya: agree. I'll spin a bench-run against current canary nodes (1k requests, seq 64/128/256 split) and collect flamegraphs + heap profiles. bench job queued.
bench-bot: scheduled perf job #2987 for canary subset (model=redwood-open-7b, seeds=1000). ETA ~4m.
lucas: quick snippet from pod logs:
```
[2026-03-17T02:58:12Z] p95=312ms p50=38ms tokens=512
[2026-03-17T03:02:05Z] p95=455ms p50=42ms tokens=512
OOM killer: no
KV-cache-hit=0.91
```
maya: that's consistent with kernel allocator thrash hypothesis — p50 steady, p95 tail. please keep nodes up for profiling, don't roll back yet.
oliver: ok let's hold the canary rollout. @deploy-bot can you pause further canary promotions and mark this canary as "hold"? also set alert to page if p95 > 1.3x baseline.
deploy-bot: canary promotion paused. label set: canary=hold. alert rule updated.
kevin: I'll add a traffic-split change to send 0% new canary traffic in eu-west, keep stable serving. Will coordinate with infra to ensure no knock-on effects.
maya: perf-run finished early. summary: baseline cluster p95=310ms, canary cluster p95=460ms. delta most pronounced for seq 128/256. flamegraph attached (uploaded to shared drive). suspect syscalls related to small-alloc path.
lucas: I can try reverting the tcmalloc flag on one canary host to A/B test. if that fixes tails we can roll a targeted fix without full rollback.
oliver: what's the risk of doing the flag revert on a single host? will it affect throughput? anyone opposed?
sara: i'm oncall lead — do not change live allocations unless we have a quick rollback path. prefer testing on a quarantined canary node first. i'll approve a single-host revert for experiment, then we evaluate metrics for 10m.
kevin: quarantine node approach sounds good. I'll cordon one node and move canary pods there.
bench-bot: perf job #2989 (post-flag-revert test) scheduled. ETA 6m.
maya: test results: reverted flag on node-17. p95 on that node: 320ms. other canary nodes still 450ms. promising.
oliver: good signal. lucas, can you prepare a patch to default the flag off for canary until we fully root cause? also open a ticket with the commit range to bisect.
lucas: creating PR to flip default for canary deployments only. will include telemetry toggles. PR: https://git.redwood/alloc/PR-421
oliver: i'll open an ops ticket to track rollback plan & postmortem.
oliver: ticket #OPS-9123 created: "canary tail latency regression — immediate mitigation + bisect". assigning to @lucas and @maya. link: https://issues.redwood/OPS-9123
sara: approved hold and mitigation plan. I'll keep monitoring for 30m and will escalate if mitigation doesn't stabilize p95 under 1.2x baseline.
maya: note for postmortem — capture baseline flamegraphs, perf scripts, and the exact kernel flags + tcmalloc version. also sample KV cache hit rates; could be interaction.
oliver: thanks everyone. we'll only resume promotions once OPS-9123 shows green and bench numbers align. react :thumbsup: to acknowledge.
kevin: adding a short runbook note to eng-oncall/playbooks: "canary-tail-latency" with the quarantine + revert steps.
lucas: collecting profiles and adding diffs to the issue.
bench-bot: perf results posted to OPS-9123. baseline vs canary graphs attached.
oliver: closing out here for now. ping me in-thread if new signals appear. :eyes:
